title: Why is ten called a triangular number?
description: A triangle of four rows of dots holds one, two, three and four dots. The video adds the rows to get ten and shows why the number is called triangular, and Keeko's doubt, that the name tells nothing, is broken.
teaching_notes: One idea: a triangular number counts the dots of a triangle built row by row. Watch for students who treat triangular as only a name to remember.

source: How many dots are in a triangle with 4 rows, and why is the
video_script.why: The child builds a triangle of dots row by row, counts the dots as a sum, and sees that the name triangular comes from the shape.
video_script.substitution: A triangular number is the number of dots in a triangle built from rows that grow by one.
video_script.anchor: a triangle of dots with four rows, one dot in the top row and one more dot in each row below
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko says triangular is only a name with no shape behind it. The ten dots really do stack in a triangle, row on row, so the name tells the shape and the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: Ten dots, and the rows stack into a triangle

final_answer.value: 10 dots; the rows stack into a triangle
final_answer.spoken: ten dots, and the rows stack into a triangle

hold_back: 10 dots, and the rows stack into a triangle
maths_rules: the 10 dots stack in the shape of a triangle
slip: the name triangular comes from the shape of the dots
video_script.design: One idea: a triangular number counts the dots of a triangle. Assumes dot pictures. Wrong idea: triangular is only a name. The triangle stays on the board to the end.

beats.on_screen: a small title card From your book; four empty rows in a stack, the top row with room for 1 dot and each row below with room for one more

marks.book: the title card From your book appears
marks.rows: four empty rows appear in a stack
marks.ask: the words how many dots and why triangular appear

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about a stack of dots.
<bookmark mark='rows'/>There are four rows, and each row is one dot longer than the row above.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>How many dots are there, and why is this number called triangular?

beats.on_screen: the empty rows hold still and the question stays on the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

beats.on_screen: a single dot, then two rows of dots, then three rows, each stack drawn smaller than the one before

marks.grow: a second and a third row are added under it, each one dot longer

narration: <bookmark mark='dot'/>We start with one dot at the top.
<bookmark mark='grow'/>Then each new row is one dot longer than the row above, and the rows pile up.

beats.on_screen: Given: a stack of dots with 4 rows
narration: <bookmark mark='given'/>Given, a stack of dots with four rows.

beats.on_screen: To find: the number of dots, and why it is called triangular

marks.find: the words number of dots and why triangular are written

narration: <bookmark mark='find'/>We have to count the dots, and find why the number is called triangular.

beats.on_screen: Step 1, fill the rows: 1 dot, 2 dots, 3 dots, 4 dots

marks.rows: the four rows fill with 1, 2, 3 and 4 dots

narration: <bookmark mark='rows'/>Step one, fill the rows. The first row has one dot and the second has two. The third has three, and the fourth has four.

marks.sum: the sum 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 = 10 is written under the rows

narration: <bookmark mark='sum'/>Step two, add the rows. One plus two plus three plus four is ten.

beats.on_screen: Step 3, look at the shape: an outline is drawn around the dots and it is a triangle

marks.outline: a triangle outline is drawn around the stack of dots

narration: <bookmark mark='outline'/>Step three, look at the shape. Draw a line around the stack. The outline is a triangle, so the number of dots is named after it.

beats.on_screen: Answer: 10 dots, and the rows stack into a triangle
narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>Ten dots, and the rows stack into a triangle. That is why ten is called a triangular number.

beats.on_screen: Keeko with a raised hand beside the boxed answer
narration: <bookmark mark='hand'/>Keeko has raised a hand. Let us check the doubt and solve it.

beats.on_screen: Keeko's doubt in a bubble; the triangle of ten dots glows with its outline; the bubble is struck through

marks.shape: the triangle outline around the ten dots glows

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks triangular is only a name, with no shape behind it.
<bookmark mark='shape'/>But the ten dots really do stack in a triangle, row on row.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>The name tells us the shape that the dots make.
